**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate uv from the caller's project**

When `dispatch.sh` is invoked from a directory containing an untrusted `pyproject.toml`, both `uv run` forms discover and synchronize that caller-controlled project before the task is validated; a local build backend can therefore execute during this probe. `uv run --help` defines `--no-project` as “Avoid discovering the project or workspace,” but it is omitted here. Add `--no-project` to both the offline and fallback forms (or run from a fixed trusted directory); otherwise the threat-table claim that the caller's working directory controls nothing is false.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/aeb4a0fbe9c4e88b6d95a4f3aa91f1f85e52d601/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run uv outside the caller-controlled directory**

When `dispatch.sh` is invoked from an untrusted directory containing `.python-version` with a path such as `./pwn`, both commands still let uv execute that caller-controlled interpreter with the orchestrator's credentials before validating the task. Fresh evidence beyond the earlier `pyproject.toml` report is that uv 0.7.22 executes `./pwn` even with `run --no-project`, while `uv help run` says `--no-project` still uses a virtual environment “found in a current or parent directory”; the existing uv test shim also models `.python-version` execution at `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_tools.py:40-43`. Run these commands from the trusted script root or resolve and pin a trusted interpreter first; the current behavior also contradicts the threat-table residual claiming the caller cwd chooses nothing.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/57d3577ca780248f573fd26c4fa460e2b5e2d510/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate the PyYAML probe from inherited Python paths**

When a trusted invocation inherits `PYTHONPATH` pointing to a caller-writable directory containing `yaml.py`, this probe runs `python -c 'import yaml'` without isolated mode, so uv preserves the variable and executes that module before the task is validated. I confirmed this behavior with uv 0.7.22; the later `python -I` calls do not prevent the initial execution. Use `python -I -c 'import yaml'` for the probe or remove Python override variables as part of the sanitized environment; otherwise the task's environment-input residual does not close this trust boundary.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/6ae8cf75df74bb54eb3b724ea7c94e16b70759ef/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore caller-controlled uv configuration**

When the caller can set `HOME` to a writable directory, both uv invocations discover `$HOME/.config/uv/uv.toml` because the clean environment preserves that value and neither command uses `--no-config`. I confirmed with uv 0.7.22 that a user config containing an `index-url` redirects the `pyyaml` fetch; a malicious index can therefore supply code that executes at the subsequent `import yaml` before the task is validated. `uv help run` documents that `--no-config` avoids configuration files normally discovered in user configuration directories, so add it to both command forms or pin a trusted HOME. This leaves the task's environment-input residual ineffective.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L78-L78](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/blob/9f6c5cebd23592793f3ad5247a20753aff26f388/AGENTS.md#L78-L78)

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Warm PyYAML before exercising the real uv wrapper**

On a clean unit-test runner, this case cannot use the stated “reachable index”: `dispatch.sh` now always invokes `uv run --offline --with pyyaml`, and `uv help run` defines `--offline` as “Disable network access.” The required Unit test workflow disables uv cache restoration and proceeds directly to `make unit-test`, which does not warm PyYAML, so the new cases exit 2 at the probe rather than reaching their assertions; this is reproducible with an empty cache. Warm the cache in the unit-test setup or make the fixture provision PyYAML independently.
